Product, scope and vocabulary

Whiteboard helps a student find academic work, complete it, know it was received and understand released feedback. It helps an instructor organize a course, assess work and publish trustworthy results. It helps a TA complete explicitly assigned teaching/grading work without inheriting the instructor's authority.

Academic web scope

Include institution sign-in handoff and arrival, role/course context, courses and archives, syllabus/modules/materials, assignments and group assignments, supported quizzes, submissions and receipts, rubrics/grading/release, learner course grades, configurable grading policy, announcements/discussions, academic calendars/private planning, TA allocation/deadlines, tools access, account/search/help, scoped attendance/insights and course copy/content import/export.

The new package expands incomplete academic workflows identified in the coworker review. It contains a proposed full design inventory, not a first-school deployment commitment. Files can become components, subroutes or page variants later, but a layout consolidation must preserve every listed task and state. Renaming a page does not justify dropping its fields, privacy or recovery rules.

Exclude campus life/organizations, event booking, registrar timetable optimization, advising/case work, financial/clinical/official SIS records, university administration, a direct-message inbox, live video conferencing, native iOS/Android and autonomous final grading. An academic calendar may display institution-owned class meetings as a read-only source; it does not grant a professor permission to edit registrar records. Existing broader designs remain untouched.

Achievements and a course FAQ assistant have optional specifications so the ideas are not lost. Do not implement them in the first required academic build. Secure-browser/proctoring support is discovery only. Tab/window state cannot prove cheating, and no automatic attempt cancellation is proposed.

Product language

TermExact meaning
Course offeringOne course in one institution/term/section context, not the reusable catalog title.
EnrollmentA person's course-scoped role and access window. One person may hold different roles in different courses.
ModuleOrdered course unit with publication, availability and prerequisite rules.
AssessmentAssignment or quiz with a stable ID, published instructions, dates, allowed attempts and grading policy mapping.
Due date / close dateDue marks expected completion; close stops ordinary new submissions. Allowances can change personal dates.
Grading deadlineA staff work target; it is independent of student due/close dates.
DraftEditable local/sample work that has not been received.
ReceivedA specific attempt accepted into the sample course record with receipt and versioned contents.
GradedReview is complete in staff scope. It is not necessarily visible to the learner.
ReleasedA specific approved score/comment/rubric snapshot is visible to its learner recipients.
MissingNo accepted work after close under the course's rule; distinguish from ungraded, excused and an interrupted upload.
ExcusedThe assessment is removed from the applicable denominator. It is not zero.
Group set / groupA named cohort partition for a task, and its named member subset. Course sections and TA grading allocations are separate concepts.
ActivityNotices about an underlying academic record; reading/dismissing a notice does not change that record.
ToolA course/institution-approved external resource, with access requirements. A link does not create a software license.
Proposed defaultA concrete starting decision for the first HTML; still revisable by the owner/institution.

Use “Instructor” in UI, with professor understood as the same role here. Use “Teaching assistant” on permission-sensitive screens. Use learner only in staff explanations where useful; “Your grades” suits student navigation.

Content and assessment bounds

First HTML uses rich text with headings, lists, links, images/alternatives, math text, attachments and video placeholders with captions/transcripts. Do not promise collaborative document editing. File requirements are configurable sample data; fixture limits are not permanent product limits.

Quiz design focuses on single-choice, multiple-select, numeric and written-response items. Imported unsupported types must become visible exceptions, not silently altered questions. Essay/file upload through assignments remains a separate path. High-stakes exam lockdown, adaptive tests, plagiarism verdicts and automatic grading of arbitrary handwriting are not implied.

Meeting links may open a plainly labeled external institution tool. The web app does not create a meeting service. Office hours can be recurring course calendar events; appointment booking is a later scoped decision, not an accidental promise.

Evidence and product status

The previous 100 designs were accepted as designs. New proposals here have not received that same acceptance. Public competitor documentation verifies that particular workflows exist, not that every school needs them or that Whiteboard is easier. Validate with the owner and a real institutional partner before setting production scope, retention, assessment rules, integrations, AI processing or operating promises.
